    How much is Rick Pitino making at St. John's?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Rick Pitino is currently in the third year of a six-year, roughly $20 million contract signed with St. John's in 2023, paying him around $3.3-$3.5 million annually. As of March 2026, reports indicate St. John's is restructuring this deal to increase his salary, aiming to make him the second-highest-paid coach in the Big East. 
    Contract Details 
    • Contract Duration: Six years (signed March 2023).
    • Total Value: Approximately $20 million.
    • Annual Salary: Reported around $3.3–$3.5 million per year.
    • Structure: The contract includes a, "substantial," salary pool for assistants. 
    Upcoming Changes (As of March 2026) 
    • St. John's has offered to restructure the remaining three years of his deal to raise his compensation, according to Newsday and National Today.
    • This move aims to make him the second-highest-paid coach in the Big East behind UConn's Dan Hurley.
    • The deal is designed to keep Pitino at St. John's long-term to reach 1,000 career wins, according to National Today. 
    Comparison 
    • At approximately $3.3M-$3.5M, he is in the middle of the pack of Big East coaching salaries.
    • This is a significant decrease from his salary at Louisville, where he earned approximately $7.7 million annually, notes Diario AS.
